quarterly_data.signal: Murphy sized the data center ramp beyond the reported segment: in calendar 2023 Marvell did about $2.2 billion in data center revenue, and next year he is looking at $15 billion-$16 billion of data center revenue. He also contrasted the plan he laid out a year ago at the same conference (about $9.5 billion in fiscal 2027 and $11 billion-plus in fiscal 2028) with today's $12 billion and $18 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: calendar 2023 data center revenue about $2.2 billion; next year $15 billion-$16 billion; year-ago plan of $9.5 billion / $11 billion now $12 billion / $18 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: over the past year the supply chain has been able to flex up 50%, taking the two-year revenue plan from $20 billion to $30 billion. Marvell reaches production more than 90%-plus of the time on first-pass silicon on advanced nodes. TSMC remains the sole-source fab vendor, with long-term deals also struck on substrate and back-end capacity plus capex and prepays. Murphy spent a week in Asia with existing and new suppliers ahead of the October 6 Investor Day; conditions are very acute right now in some areas, and he warned that some substrate capacity cannot be obtained until the end of the decade by anyone who did not start five years ago.
quarterly_data.figure: supply chain flexed up 50%; two-year plan from $20 billion to $30 billion; 90%-plus first-pass silicon success on advanced node

quarterly_data.signal: Murphy named Google on stage as the counterparty of the SEC 8-K warrant filed before the Q2 call and characterised it as an XPU-attach relationship rather than an XPU socket, covering NICs, CXL, storage controllers, near memory compute and AI acceleration. He stressed that Marvell is running the same playbook across the whole spectrum of hyperscale customers for programs that have no warrant or 8-K attached, so their size is not public, and that XPU-attach products are largely Marvell's own IP built to spec with the customer's name on the chip.

Mix behind the raise: when next year's revenue outlook was still like $13.5 billion, custom was about the same size as it is today; the raise from $13.5 billion to $18 billion came mostly from interconnect and switching and storage, with only some from custom. Durn expects operating margin to walk from touching the low end of the 38%-40% range this Q4 to touching the high end next year at a similar range of gross margin, and Murphy expects gross margin flat-ish next year with operating margin expansion even though custom doubles, because custom NRE is booked as contra R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: next-year revenue raised from $13.5 billion to $18 billion, mostly interconnect/switching/storage; gross margin flat-ish with operating margin from the low end to the high end of 38%-40%

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up optics raised for a second time in two weeks: a quarter ago the next-fiscal-year outlook was zero to $300 million, on the Q2 call Murphy said it would be much higher, and at Citi he told investors to imagine that number is even greater, with NPO and scale-up optics a big part of the guide-up. Marvell already sells TIAs and drivers into third-party NPO modules built for hyperscalers, which he called a billion-dollar business for us already just on analog components, and said Marvell content is very high in the NPO module ecosystem with TIAs and drivers. NPO and CPO will coexist rather than replace each other, with a big NPO ramp in calendar 2028 and 2029 as CPO layers in.
quarterly_data.figure: next-year scale-up optics: prior guide zero to $300 million, now greater still; TIAs and drivers a billion-dollar business for us already just on analog components

quarterly_data.signal: DCI at 1.6T: Marvell was first to market announcing 2nm DSPs that go inside the module, bring-up has been excellent and the silicon photonics platform is tracking well, backed by 15 billion device hours of reliability data. Marvell builds the modules itself and is investing in its own module manufacturing capacity while also selling the DSPs to third-party module makers. Management cited market estimates that scale-across could 2, 3, 4, 5x the size of the DCI market on top of the ASP-per-generation growth DCI already delivers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2nm DSP first to market; 15 billion device hours of reliability data; scale-across could 2, 3, 4, 5x the size of the DCI market
